answer: Because the timing is recorded against the timber challenge, the comet audit can replay the shale history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 225 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. A scripted farm thus has to pad 184 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
